facts.fact: 70-seat restaurant that also caters weddings and office events at customers' venues with a small catering crew; nine employees; books kept by an outside accountant
The owner, Rosa Delacroix, has filed an election of exclusion and is not on the payroll register
The catering lead and her two crew members prepare event food in the restaurant kitchen and serve it at the venue; on quiet weeks they work restaurant shifts
The owner's sales summary splits monthly receipts between the dining room and off-site catering

open_items.about: Catering crew restaurant shifts (Hannah Pryor, Ivan Petrov, Clara Bose)
open_items.proposal: Keep each catering crew member's whole pay under F-720, as the employer reported.
open_items.why: The field notes say the catering crew works restaurant shifts on quiet weeks, but the file has no time record showing how many. House practice does not split one person's pay between codes, except for route ride-alongs (HP-2), and their main work is catering (CG-42). If their records showed mostly restaurant shifts, the code would change.

open_items.about: Gross receipts not used to split payroll
open_items.proposal: Do not allocate payroll from gross-receipts.csv.
open_items.why: Premium is based on payroll (CG-01, CG-03). Receipts are sales, and house practice gives no rule for using them to divide payroll. The receipts are noted only as context: off-site catering is about 22% of receipts.
